rationale: The workflow already implements the evidence-supported optimizations that fit it: dependency downloads are cached via `prefix-dev/setup-pixi` with `cache: true` in all three jobs (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE), and superseded runs are cancelled via `concurrency.cancel-in-progress` (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE). A pip-level `actions/cache` addition is inapplicable because the workflow installs Python dependencies through pixi, not pip, and pixi does not use `~/.cache/pip`; adding it would be an unrelated, unsupported change. P-LIT-FAIL-FAST is contraindicated because `fail-fast: false` is intentionally set to preserve every matrix outcome across ubuntu/macos/windows. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT lacks a precondition: there is no representative per-job successful-duration history to set a safe limit, and imposing one risks killing valid slow runs (e.g., the LaTeX/TinyTex installation step). No schedule trigger exists to suppress (P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE/P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE), and no history-based job gating is supported by CI service evidence. Preserving all build/test coverage, no supported minimal change remains.
